(Search snippet content — full article inaccessible on direct fetch (repeated ETIMEDOUT); ITV News reporting language via web search.)

Published 28 July 2026. Burnham to unveil plans to make new technical education routes available to 14-year-olds to tackle rising youth unemployment; PM said he is on "a mission" to curb the rise of NEETs, now more than one million. Bursary of up to £4,500 to help teenagers in universal credit households take up an apprenticeship (addresses a "benefits cliff-edge"); up to £8,000 support for SMEs hiring young apprentices; part-funded via the £1bn additional Growth and Skills Levy investment announced in May. He did not set a date for getting NEET numbers falling.

Youth benefit conditionality (reported across ITV/PA and corroborated by IFS): those aged 16-24 out of work for at least 18 months would be given a job offer they would have to take; those who decline without a reasonable excuse could face sanctions, including a reduction in benefits.

REACTION QUOTES:
Lib Dem education spokesperson Munira Wilson: the plan "must come in with built-in safeguards to allow young people the flexibility to retrospectively change direction and move between 'academic' and 'technical'" and "We must not allow these changes to predetermine children's futures at just 14, baking in disadvantage."
NAHT general secretary Paul Whiteman: schools "will need much greater clarity about what it means in practice and over funding."

Prior warning (Bloomberg, 27 July 2026): Labour MPs (Socialist Campaign Group) warned Burnham he would lose party support if he pursued "punitive" welfare cuts.
